problems: The 'ring' never reads as a ring: in every storyboard frame and all three full-size frames it is a straight diagonal streak of coloured balls coming out of the top-left corner and ending in mid-air above the trees. No curve, no arc over the island, nothing that closes or comes back round.

'Going round' isn't visible: the streak sits in roughly the same place on screen from the first frame to the last while the camera drifts, so it looks pasted onto the sky rather than orbiting. No ball can be seen travelling along it.

'Then Pinchy went up too' isn't shown: the crab stands on the ground at the right in storyboard frames 1-4, leaves the picture as the camera pans away (frames 5-10), and only a tiny orange speck in the sky appears from frame 11 on (ring-at-75, right of the pines). The lift-off is never on screen, and the speck is too small to recognise as Pinchy.

The caption names the things in the ring as stuff that was 'kicked, splashed and bonked too hard', but nothing in the film shows any of them being kicked or launched. The balls are anonymous dots with no visible link to the island's games.
The streak ends abruptly in mid-air above the treeline (ring-at-25, ring-at-50) and doesn't continue behind or around anything, so it looks cut off.

Framing: what matters is squeezed into the top-left corner and a speck at the upper right, while most of the frame is the same meadow and trees. In the second half the camera drifts into an empty foreground, with nothing happening there.
posts.critique: Someone who doesn't know the island sees a frozen diagonal line of beads in the sky over a pleasant meadow: not a ring, nothing visibly going round, and no crab going up. The caption tells a story the pictures don't show.
